medSchoolStudLife.diversity:
The education, research and patient care mission of EVMS is shaped by many considerations: the demographics of the surrounding communities, the significant presence of military personnel, retirees and their families, the rural and underserved communities of the Commonwealth of Virginia, and the broader national and global need to address gaps in the health workforce and healthcare accessibility.
Macon & Joan Brock Virginia Health Sciences -EVMS at Old Dominion University is committed to fostering an environment that attracts and supports individuals with a wide range of experiences, perspectives, and talents. By expanding access to education and professional opportunities, we strengthen innovation, excellence, and equity in healthcare. As the needs of our communities and the healthcare landscape evolve, we will continue to cultivate a culture of inclusion, engagement, and opportunity for all.
medSchoolStudLife.leaveOfAbsence: A leave of absence may be granted with approval of either the Associate Dean for Student Affairs or Vice Dean of Academic Affairs.  A leave of absence will be granted for up to 12 months.  In exceptional circumstances, consideration will be given for an extension, up to a maximum of 24 months.  At the end of the requested leave of absence, the student must return or is considered to have withdrawn for financial aid purposes.
medSchoolStudLife.organizationActivities: As a school of medicine and health professions that was founded by the community for the community, EVMS students are actively engaged in over 50 student organizations and interest groups built on community partnerships and service.  EVMS has received several national and regional awards for its commitment to community service and strives to be the most community-oriented school of medicine and health professions in the nation. The EVMS Service Learning and Global Health Programs in the Office of Academic Affairs, the M. Foscue Brock Institute for Community & Global Health, and Office of Student Affairs support student initiatives in our local, national, and international communities. EVMS students and faculty support the first student-run free clinic in the state of Virginia, addressing access to quality healthcare for uninsured Norfolk residents while enhancing the educational experience of students and building capacity to serve communities experiencing widespread health inequities.
medSchoolStudLife.setting: Macon & Joan Brock Virginia Health Sciences Eastern Virginia Medical School (VHS-EVMS) at Old Dominion University campus complex includes the Children's Hospital of the Kings Daughters and Sentara Norfolk General Hospital.  The campus is minutes from downtown shopping areas and cultural attractions.
medSchoolStudLife.housing:
VHS-EVMS Campus at Old Dominion University has campus housing. where you will find 1 bedroom, 2 bedroom and 1 bedroom loft style apartments, directly across the street from the EVMS campus. Located on the corner of Colley Avenue and across from Lewis Hall, our student housing community offers you all the conveniences of home offering both furnished and unfurnished apartments.

With the convenience of on-campus living, and by creating a worry-free, quiet learning environment to match, our goal is to support you in making your academic experience a success. It's not just about having a great apartment, it's about giving you the resources you need to succeed, with a college experience you'll treasure.

Confirmed students can contact Campus Housing at 757.446.5961, CampusHousing@evms.edu or https://www.evmscampushousing.com/floor-plans
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystems: At VHS-EVMS, we are happy to help build a community of inclusion with our Safe Zone Program.  Safe Zone promotes the support of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender and questioning/queer (LGBTQ) students, staff, faculty and residents through education and training to establish identifiable allies who are supportive, trustworthy, and sensitive to the needs of LGBTQ individuals.  This program aims to make our campus a safer and more accepting environment for all members of a community, regardless of gender identity and sexual orientation.
medSchoolStudLife.supportSystemsForDisabilities: Student Disability Services works individually with students who have an identified disability to determine any disability related barriers to the educational environment and determine reasonable accommodations to address those barriers to provide equal access to their education.
medSchoolStudLife.wellnessPrograms:
https://www.odu.edu/virginia-health-sciences/community-engaged-learning/student-health-wellness
The Wellness Program at EVMS is an integrated approach to assist specifically with student health and their well-being.  To achieve academic success, students must be physically and mentally well and learn within a low-stress environment.
medSchoolStudLife.campusCulture:
VHS-EVMS will be recognized as the most community-oriented school of medicine and health professions in the United States.

As a student and community facing institution three core values drive our daily efforts:
Excellence: We determine with our stakeholders what is valuable and hold ourselves to high performance standards that fulfill our promises.

Collegiality: We serve our community and one another, building strong and mutually supportive relationships. We work as a cooperative, united team to further our purposes of education, research and patient care.

Integrity: We strive to maintain the highest ethical standards and accept accountability for all we do and say.

medSchoolCurriculum.dressCode: Students are required to follow the dress code of the site where they are rotating.
medSchoolCurriculum.tutoringPrograms: Academic Development supports medical students’ academic achievement through personal counseling, peer-to-peer tutoring, workshops on success strategies, and preparation for USMLE exams.
medSchoolCurriculum.patientInteraction: EVMS pioneered the use of standardized patients over 20 years ago. The program is a resource that provides invaluable training to medical students giving early access to realistic patient experiences.
medSchoolCurriculum.instructionStyle: Instruction style consists of didactic lectures, small group sessions and team-centered learning.
medSchoolCurriculum.clinicalRotations: Rotations are conducted at Sentara Norfolk General Hospital unless otherwise indicated.
medSchoolCurriculum.lectureAttendance: No attendance policy for the vast majority of classes, however, there are some mandatory lectures in some courses.
medSchoolCurriculum.curricularHighlights:
The CareForward Curriculum was designed to enhance learning through integration and innovation. It is a modular, fully integrated, organ-systems and case-based curriculum that includes individual disciplines and longitudinal themes: caring for the elderly and those with multiple chronic conditions, cost-conscious care, service learning, and student and physician wellness.

The first 2 years, now condensed to 18 months, provide early clinical exposure through high-fidelity simulation and physician shadowing, many in community-based practices. VHS-EVMS redesigned its curriculum to support student growth and continued success while adapting to changes in medical education and future clinical practice. We remain unequivocally committed to developing caring, compassionate, clinically proficient, culturally humble, community-oriented physicians.

The new design allows for:
Increased time for students to practice and develop clinical skills across the entire curriculum
Additional time for elective phase rotations
Earlier start to clinical clerkships
Accelerated pre-clerkship phase (achieved via refining the sequence and delivery of content)
Refined vertical integration of curriculum and assessment
Enhanced coaching of student skillsets within and across phases of the MD program
Preserved dedicated study time for USMLE Step 1 preparation while increasing dedicated time for Step 2 preparation
Increased time for preparation for components of residency applications

Third-year clerkships provide ambulatory and inpatient experiences across diverse settings with exposure to core specialties, geriatric medicine, addiction medicine, and surgical and medical subspecialties. Fourth-year electives are diverse & allow exploration of special interests, including research and subspecialty care. Grades are Honors, High Pass, Pass, or Fail for all clinical rotations.
medSchoolCurriculum.primaryCarePrograms: VHS-EVMS students have several opportunities to experience primary care medicine in the curriculum.  In the very popular Longitudinal Generalist Mentorship Program first and second year students spend at least 7 afternoons each semester working in the office of a practicing primary care physician.  Third year students rotate through the required Clerkship in Family and Community Medicine and fourth year students have several primary care electives from which to choose.  The student run free clinic, the HOPES Clinic, an excellent model for primary care, is located in the local health department, serving the indigent population of Norfolk.  The Family Medicine Interest Group is dedicated to promoting family medicine and primary care in general as a career choice.
medSchoolCurriculum.researchPrograms: Research involving medical students and residents has grown steadily at EVMS and is an integral part of the medical school's mission of educating medical professionals and improving health care. The research receives support from a variety of foundations, state and federal sponsors, including the NIH. Currently, there are over one hundred faculty conducting basic, clinical and population health research at EVMS focused on community healthcare needs, ranging from diabetes, maternal and infant health to cancer and infectious diseases.  To accelerate research in population health and management, EVMS has established the Institute for Healthcare Analytics and Discovery Science, which presents new research opportunities to learners at EVMS.  Additional research is conducted in geriatrics, head and neck surgery, ophthalmology, pediatrics, reproductive medicine, and sleep medicine. The research stresses interdisciplinary collaboration with teams of basic and clinical scientists.
medSchoolCurriculum.communityServiceText: A mandatory service learning course has a required community activity component.
medSchoolCurriculum.affiliatedHospitals: VHS-EVMS works in partnership with hospitals, physicians, and clinics throughout the region, providing students with a broad base of clinical experience.
medSchoolCurriculum.gradingSystem:
M1/M2 - Pass/Fail
M3/M4 - Honors, High Pass, Pass and Fail

medSchoolInformation.generalInformation: In the 1960s, civic leaders in Hampton Roads sought to improve care in the region and created a bold dream to build a medical school. Thanks to determination and community commitment, EVMS opened its doors in 1973, forever transforming the landscape of health care in Hampton Roads.  Established to enhance the quality and diversity of health care throughout the region, the mission is deeply rooted in the education and training of primary care physicians, arming them with the requisite scientific, academic, and humanistic skills most relevant to today's practice of medicine. VHS-EVMS graduates provide health care for more than one quarter of Virginia's population as well as neighboring regions of North Carolina and is the place for aspiring physicians and health professionals, passionate educators and medical pioneers.  EVMS holds an honored position in American history as one of the only schools of medicine and health professions in the nation to be founded by a grassroots effort.
medSchoolInformation.missionStatement: Macon & Joan Brock Virginia Health Sciences Eastern Virginia Medical School (VHS-EVMS) at Old Dominion University is an academic health center dedicated to achieving excellence in medical and health professions education, research and patient care. We value creating and fostering a diverse and cohesive faculty, professional staff and student body as the surest way to achieve our mission. Adhering to the highest ethical standards, we will strive to improve the health of our community and to be recognized as a national center of intellectual and clinical strength in medicine and Health Professions. Our commitment to ensuring institutional effectiveness is demonstrated by the continuous assessment processes we use to improve program performance and student learning outcomes.
medSchoolInformation.programUndergradCollege: Christopher Newport University, Hampden-Sydney College, Hampton University, Norfolk State University, Old Dominion University, Virginia Wesleyan University, the College of William & Mary, Virginia State University, Virginia Military Institute, and Virginia Union University.
medSchoolInformation.programAbout:
Students applying have already been accepted to VHS-EVMS at the end of their sophomore year of college.

This program exists to offer outstanding and qualified undergraduate students with firm interests in a career as a physician and in attending VHS-EVMS the opportunity to gain early assurance of acceptance into the MD program at VHS-EVMS before beginning their final year of college. By granting early assurance of acceptance into the program, sophomore students will be able to broaden their academic focus, engage in extracurricular leadership activities and pursue first-hand direct patient care experience.
medSchoolInformation.videoDescription: Six aspiring physicians share how VHS-EVMS and Hampton Roads have shaped their education — and how they intend to pay their positive experiences forward.

medSchoolApplication.matricNote: Note: EVMS is no longer able to accept applications from international applicants.
medSchoolApplication.amcasLettersText:
IF YOUR GRADUATE PROGRAM HAS NOT STARTED, you must send a letter from the program verifying your enrollment and the completion date. 
NOTE: APPLICATIONS ARE HELD UNTIL ALL REQUIRED LETTERS ARE RECEIVED.
You may send more letters beyond the required minimum if you choose up to the maximum letters allowed.  A committee letter serves as one letter.
medSchoolApplication.letterGuidance:
ALL LETTERS MUST BE ON LETTERHEAD & SIGNED BY THE WRITER. 
If your undergraduate/graduate institution has a premedical committee, we strongly recommend sending a committee letter. You can also send letters through your career services office, and this can serve as a committee letter. If a committee letter is not available, you must send three individual letters:  2 letters from faculty in natural sciences, neuroscience or research, 1 letter from a non-science faculty.  Mathematics fall under the non-science category. The non-science faculty letter can be substituted with a letter from an employer, mentor, physician or a volunteer/clinical experience).  
Graduate Applicants:
Applicants currently or previously enrolled in a Graduate Program must send an ADDITIONAL LETTER (4th letter) from their thesis/graduate advisor (unless sending a graduate committee letter).
medSchoolApplication.videoInterview: Yes, via ZOOM must have a working camera.
medSchoolApplication.acceptOutstateApplInformation: We accept up to 49 percent of out-of -state applicants.
medSchoolApplication.acceptCanadianApplInformation: Applicants can attend Canadian schools; however, they must be US citizens.
medSchoolApplication.additionalInfo:
The MCAT is a computer-based exam that is offered multiple times throughout the year and must be taken by the prospective student before the application can be processed.
VHS-Eastern Virginia Medical School will accept test scores taken from January 2024 to September 2026, for the 2026-2027 admissions cycle.
The MCAT tests academic competencies in the natural sciences, reasoning and analysis skills, and concepts from psychology, sociology, and biology that provide the foundation for learning in medical school about the behavioral and socio-cultural determinants of health, according to the AAMC. An applicant may wish to take the MCAT more than once to ensure the best possible performance. If an applicant intends to take the MCAT for the first time in the fall, a review of his or her application will not take place until the score has been received. Information and registration may be accessed online.
medSchoolApplication.mcatScoresAdditionalInfo: The MD Admissions Committee looks at the highest score and the number of times taken.
medSchoolApplication.gpaScreenAdditionalInfo: GPAs should be near or above our average to be considered a competitive applicant.  Our average cumulative and BCPM GPAs are ~3.6.
medSchoolApplication.minUndergradGpaInfo: VHS-EVMS acknowledges that applicants who complete these programs seek to demonstrate their ability to meet the demands of medical school.  As a result, we carefully evaluate their academic performance beyond undergraduate school.  Rather than a fixed minimum GPA, the MD Admissions Committee has a holistic approach, considering all coursework and grades in an assessment.
medSchoolApplication.minCreditHourInfo: The minimum required credit hours vary, since program structures and completion requirements differ.  Additionally, some applicants pursue post-baccalaureate coursework independently when a formal program does not align with their specific goals and needs.  Applicants who have completed at least 24 credit hours are often times considered competitive.
medSchoolApplication.courseworkAcceptanceInfo: VHS-EVMS accepts coursework taken at community colleges.
medSchoolApplication.letterOfIntentAdditionalInfo: Letters should come from applicants who are waitlisted.
medSchoolApplication.technicalStandardInfo: Students who graduate from the MD program must be prepared for entry into the practice of medicine within post-graduate medical education training programs. As such, in addition to meeting academic criteria, each applicant to and student in the MD program must demonstrate that they possess independent ability, aptitude, and skills to meet the non-academic criteria. These Technical Standards must be met with or without accommodation and are essential for admission to, promotion within and graduation from the MD program.  They are as follows: Observation Skills Technical Standard, Communication Skills Technical Standard, Critical Reasoning Skills Technical Standard, Motor and Sensory Function Technical Standard, and Behavioral and Social Attributes Technical Standard.  For more detailed information you can click the link below.

medSchoolFinancial.financialAid: Students seeking financial aid must complete both the Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) at www.fafsa.gov & the EVMS Online Financial Aid Application, which will be available online after February 1 for accepted students. Additional forms or information may be requested as needed. EVMS financial aid is comprised of federal loans, need based grants for qualified state residents, & institutional scholarships and loans.  Federal loans will assist students in fully meeting their cost of attendance providing they meet all federal criteria, including citizenship requirements, are credit worthy (for Graduate PLUS Loan), & maintain satisfactory academic progress. Students are encouraged to review the financial aid website for the Application Process and Types of Aid. EVMS also participates in Title VII federal aid for HRSA Primary Care Loans (for those interested in an approved primary care field of study) & Loans for Disadvantaged Students (for those who meet the criteria).
medSchoolFinancial.tuitionPolicy: Tuition and fees are due by the first day of classes.  Accounts are considered past due if not paid in full by the close of business on the first day of classes. Unpaid account balances after 30 days from the start of classes are considered delinquent and the student will be suspended from academic activities if not paid.

medSchoolPrograms.info:
Master of Science degree in Biomedical Sciences - Medical is a pre-professional (post-baccalaureate) master’s degree program designed for students who wish to matriculate into medical school and can be completed in a one-year or two-year curriculum track. It provides an opportunity for motivated students to improve their academic credentials by demonstrating their academic abilities in a rigorous medical school environment. It is particularly suitable to help students make themselves more competitive applicants to any medical program.
***Program Highlights
Program lets participants learn side-by-side with medical school students in the classroom and the lab.
Mentorship opportunities allow participants to be paired with a first-year medical student who have completed the program.
Program completion aims to help students become more academically competitive and an overall better candidate for admission to the professional school of their choice.

medSchoolTimeline.eventDetail: Feb. 19 - April 15: Accepted applicants may select the "Plan to Enroll" option in AMCAS.
Accepted applicants should narrow their offers of acceptance to three medical schools.

Accepted applicants will have two options to select: “Plan to Enroll” or “Commit to Enroll.” Selecting “Commit to Enroll” indicates that the applicant has made a final selection and has withdrawn from all other medical schools.
Accepted students are required to select the "Commit to Enroll" option in AMCAS. If commit to enroll is not selected by July 15, your offer of acceptance may be rescinded.

medSchoolMdPathway.programDesc: Launched in January 2026, the EVMS @ ODU Accelerated MD (AMP) Program enables select students to earn their MD in just three years, with a direct pathway to match into the EVMS @ ODU Emergency Medicine Residency. Students begin in January of their M1 year with the longitudinal Research Scholars course with mentorship by Emergency Medicine faculty. AMP students benefit from early specialty immersion as well as completion of all required specialty clerkships, preparing them for residency success.
medSchoolMdPathway.eligibleApplicants:
Applicants must:
· Be an enrolled EVMS medical students in good academic standing
· Successfully completed all previous coursework without failure
· Have no honor code or professionalism violations
· Meet all institutional requirements for promotion and graduation
· Be prepared to complete the 3-year curriculum without interruption
· Be committed to pursuing Emergency Medicine residency training
medSchoolMdPathway.applicationProcess: Applications will be solicited by the EVMS @ ODU Office of Undergraduate Medical Education at the beginning of the M1 year. Applicants must submit a curriculum vitae and a letter of interest. Eligible candidates will be invited to interview with the AMP Selection Committee. Final selections will be made during the first week of December 2026.
medSchoolMdPathway.programRestReq:
· Currently limited to students committed to Emergency Medicine
· Students must complete the 3-year curriculum without interruption
· No leave of absence, research year, or dual-degree (e.g., MD/MPH) participation
· Must pass all courses, clerkships, and USMLE Step 1 & Step 2 on the first attempt
· Professionalism concerns may result in transition back to the 4-year program
· Failure to match into Emergency Medicine results in transition to the traditional 4-year pathway
medSchoolMdPathway.residencyAffiliationPathway: Directed residency option available to Three-Year MD students

medSchoolAcceptance.waitlistProcedure: The waitlist remains active until the class matriculates in August.  Updates and letters of interest are accepted.

medSchoolSelection.premedReqRec:
Biology (with labs) 1 year
General chemistry (with labs) 1 year
Organic chemistry (with labs) 1 year
Physics (with labs) 1 year
(Biochemistry is highly recommended)

Applicants must have a passing grade in all required courses. They can be in the form of a numerical, letter, or pass/fail grade. Credits earned through advanced placement programs or CLEP are acceptable. Applicants may enhance their chances of acceptance by taking graduate coursework in the natural sciences.  In recent years, students matriculating at VHS-EVMS have had a mean GPA of 3.70 and a mean MCAT of 513.
medSchoolSelection.medSchoolMediaSites: Facebook, Twitter, Google+, You Tube, Linked in and Flickr
medSchoolSelection.selectionFactors: All applicants must be US citizens or US permanent residents.  VHS-EVMS does not discriminate based on sex, race, creed, age, national origin, marital status, or handicap. A supplemental application is requested from those applicants who receive a favorable initial screening of their completed AMCAS application.  The Admissions Committee considers the entire academic record, including science (BCPM) and overall GPA, MCAT scores, exposure to the medical field, volunteerism, maturity, character, and motivation.  The application fee will be waived if a fee waiver has been granted by AMCAS.  Preference is given to legal residents of Virginia.  VHS-EVMS seeks individuals with personal and background traits that indicate a high potential for becoming a great clinician passionate about service.
medSchoolSelection.preMedShadowText: Shadowing is strongly recommended as is a letter from an physician.
